summary: The 98.43 spike is just the cut, so it isn't a fault. The slingshot barely reads: the figure is a tiny, stiff silhouette on Mars. At 100.13 the camera clips through huge dark geometry.

faults.what: The frame is filled with giant dark navy and black curved slabs and a red wedge. It looks like the camera passing through or inside geometry. The next tile (100.16) jumps to a red ridge, Jupiter and a beige sky with no transition.
faults.fix: Move the camera path or the terrain and shell meshes so the lens never enters them. Otherwise cut this frame out.

faults.what: After the cut, the hero is a tiny flat black silhouette hugging the edge of Mars. Mars fills the frame and the character is hard to find. The turkey on top is a few pixels of red and black, so 'watching from the top' doesn't read.
faults.fix: Push in on the hero and the turkey, or frame them larger, so the subject and the turkey are readable.

faults.what: From 98.46 to 98.63 the silhouette keeps the same stiff, spread-limb pose. It drifts across the face of Mars with no bank, lean, anticipation or arc, so it doesn't look like a hard slingshot turn.
faults.fix: Bank the figure into the curve, add a pose change or lean through the turn, and move it along a clear arc around the planet.

faults.what: Mars is almost static and only swells slightly across the shot. The speed streaks on the right are the only sense of motion, so the whoosh feels weak.
faults.fix: Add a camera sweep or parallax, or make Mars slide and rotate faster as the hero passes, to sell the speed.

faults.what: From 100.26 to 100.36 the blue sphere and its cluster of rock chunks sit at the right edge, half cropped and almost still, in a flat beige empty frame.
faults.fix: Recompose so the subject sits inside the frame and add motion to the debris.
